transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-30 16:00 PST
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Raman (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (CTO, Saffron), Leo Alvarez (Head of Platform), Rina Patel (Security)

Auto-summary (auto-generated): discuss security gates and measurable POC success criteria, agree on artifacts and schedule baseline run.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time, really appreciate it. quick roll call?
[00:07] Maya: Maya here, hi.
[00:09] Leo: Leo on the call.
[00:11] Rina: Rina, hi.
[00:13] Jordan: Great. Priya from infra side is with me, she'll drive the bench plan later.
[00:18] Priya: hey all.
[00:20] Jordan: Cool. The agenda we put in the invite — security gating for the POC, success criteria and a realistic timeline, and then a benchmark plan. anything to add?
[00:28] Maya: no that's good. We're trying to be careful — payments is sensitive so we need the SOC2 and ISO story up front, and the SSO stuff.
[00:36] Jordan: Totally. Quick context check — what's the target integration? Is this a feature that will run for auth-time fraud checks, or more of an offline scoring?
[00:44] Leo: It's inline-ish. the real-time flow — we call the model on transactions, get a risk score, then apply rules. Typical latency constraints, we can't add more than ~200ms on the critical path.
[00:55] Priya: okay that helps. For a POC we usually set internal targets — p50 under 120ms, p95 under 350ms at a simulated 1k QPS workload for the feature. Does that sound in the ballpark?
[01:07] Maya: 120ms p50 is aggressive but acceptable as a pilot target, p95 350 maybe a bit high but fine for initial. Our SLA will be stricter later.
[01:16] Rina: From security, our checklist: SOC2 or equivalent, ISO 27001 summary, SSO via SAML with SP-initiated flow, SCIM for user provisioning ideally, RBAC that maps to our roles, and detailed audit logs with export to our Splunk. also KMS integration and key management details.
[01:33] Jordan: Great list. We'll send the SOC2 summary + controls mapping. For SAML we support both SP and IdP initiated flows; do you have an IdP?
[01:41] Maya: Okta.
[01:43] Jordan: Perfect, Okta is a common one. We also have SCIM support for user sync. Priya, do we have any known limitations around audit log fields?
[01:52] Priya: We can emit per-request logs with request id, model id, timestamps, token counts, and an obfuscated prompt hash if they want. full PII in prompts we mask — that's the usual pattern. Logs can stream to a customer S3 or via syslog to their SIEM. retention policy's configurable but for pilot we do 30 days by default.
[02:12] Rina: We need 90 days for the pilot for compliance review, is that doable?
[02:17] Priya: For pilot-only env we can extend to 90 days, yes. We'll note that as an action item.
[02:22] Jordan: On KMS — we support customer-managed keys via common KMS providers, we can provide an HSM-backed flow in private deployments. For hosted, we can use our managed keys but export controls and encryption-in-transit at TLS 1.3.
[02:35] Leo: if we go hosted for the pilot, are there options to pin region & restrict egress?
[02:40] Jordan: Yes, region pinning and egress rules are standard on dedicated and private. For hosted we can restrict to region and have stricter network peering, but complete egress locking is usually on private deployments.
[02:50] Maya: Our preference is hosted first to move faster but we need clear auditability and SSO. If that works for the security folks, we can do hosted pilot for 4 weeks and see throughput.
[02:59] Rina: As long as the logs and k/v of the tokens are auditable and we can get proof of SOC2 controls, hosted is okay. We do want the option to move to a VPC/private lane during pilot if something pops up.
[03:12] Priya: That's fine. we'll propose a two-phase run: baseline correctness + small load, then a sustained throughput run. For the baseline we'll run 500 requests to validate output parity against your golden set. Then a 2-hour throughput run at scaled QPS to simulate steady-state.
[03:29] Jordan: Success criteria we heard so far: latency targets, throughput, and accuracy/regression. Maya, can you share what you consider acceptable degradation in model outputs?
[03:37] Maya: We have a golden set of 2k labeled cases. For pilot we'd accept up to 1% regression on key metrics (false positive rate / false negative rate) compared to our current rule-based baseline. Any more and we can't progress.
[03:49] Priya: Noted. We'll add the regression test step to the bench plan. We'll also record token cost approximations for you — to understand cost per decision.
[03:58] Leo: on sizing: our average transaction payload is ~1.2k tokens after serialization. Peak expected QPS for this flow is ~200, but we want to plan for 1k QPS as a stress test.
[04:12] Priya: Ok that token size matters — it affects throughput and batching. For 1.2k tokens, continuous KV cache and batching require some tuning. We'll propose two profiles: tuned for low-latency (smaller batch sizes) and tuned for cost (larger batches).
[04:26] Rina: For data handling, can Redwood guarantee no persistent storage of raw inputs for hosted pilot?
[04:32] Jordan: We have request-level retention settings. For pilot we can ensure no raw prompt retention beyond short-term cache, and hashed-only logs for auditing. We'll include the retention settings in the security pack.
[04:44] Maya: Good. Also want to confirm SAML SSO + RBAC mapping. Our roles: FraudAnalyst, Ops, PlatformAdmin. We need role restrictions on model rollout and ability to revoke tokens.
[04:57] Priya: We support role mapping via SCIM groups and RBAC policies in the console. Revocation of API keys/scoped tokens is immediate in the control plane and we'll emit the revocation event to audit logs.
[05:08] Jordan: Let's talk timeline. If we get artifacts this week, we can spin up a pilot cluster next week and run benchmarks the week after. Realistically a 3-4 week pilot including verification. Is that aligned?
[05:19] Maya: Yes 3-4 weeks is fine. Security will need to review SOC docs — that's usually a 5 day turn.
[05:25] Rina: we'll try to review in 3 business days once we have the docs.
[05:29] Jordan: Great. Priya, can you outline the bench plan items quickly?
[05:32] Priya: Sure. Step one: correctness test — run your 2k golden set, measure AUC, false pos/neg, record diffs. Step two: ramp test — 0 to 200 QPS ramp over 15 mins. Step three: stress run — sustained 1k QPS for 2 hours to observe stability, tail lat, memory growth. Step four: regression & parity checks post-run. We'll capture p50/p95/p99 and error rates.
[05:55] Leo: For the stress run, we need to coordinate egress and capacity — if hosted, will you throttle?
[06:01] Priya: We'll coordinate. For hosted we have burst limits and can open capacity for the two-hour run; we just need a lead time and an expected traffic profile.
[06:09] Jordan: Pricing for the pilot — we'll share a short pilot agreement with committed hours and expected credits. Shouldn't be a major blocker.
[06:16] Maya: ok. A few security specifics: will you provide a control-plane audit log that shows who initiated model deployments and who ran which prompts?
[06:24] Jordan: Yes, control-plane logs include user-level events: deploy, rollback, policy changes. Data-plane logs cover requests. Both can be exported.
[06:33] Rina: Also need proof of pen test or third-party assessment in the last 12 months.
[06:38] Jordan: We'll include our latest third-party pen test summary and the SOC2 Type II report.
[06:42] Maya: Great. Anything else?
[06:44] Leo: One more — in the event of a regression, can you rollback to a previous model quickly?
[06:49] Priya: yes, we support pinned versions and quick rollback + automatic fallback rules. We'll demo that in the pilot.
[06:56] Jordan: OK wrapping — recap of agreed items: Jordan to send security pack (SOC2, ISO summary, pen test), Priya to send benchmark plan and runbook, Saffron to provide sample payloads and golden set, and schedule the baseline run week of Dec 13.
[07:12] Maya: yep. We'll aim to get the data by Dec 8.
[07:15] Rina: I'll review security docs and revert by Dec 4.
[07:19] Jordan: Thanks all. We'll follow up with calendar invites for the baseline run.
[07:23] Maya: thanks. bye.

End of transcript.
